source.title: Discovering Transformer Circuits via a Hybrid Attribution and Pruning Framework
source.authors: Hao Gu; V. Nair; Amrithaa Ashok Kumar; J. Sharma; Ryan Lagasse

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a different circuit-discovery approach to GPT-2 Small on IOI and reports circuit accuracy, faithfulness metrics, and which S-inhibition heads the methods retain.
record.gate_note: The study reports aggregate circuit-quality metrics for EAP, EP, and HAP, plus a qualitative comparison of S-inhibition-head retention. It does not directly ablate or patch the named heads to test their causal roles. The stated 200-example training and validation sets and 36,084-example test split are not separate outcome conditions.
record.test_reason: The study runs three automated circuit-discovery methods (EAP, EP, HAP) on GPT-2 small IOI. It scores their circuits against the Wang et al. manual circuit and reports whether the original S-inhibition heads (7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10) are recovered. That bears directly on V4, whether other methods recover essentially the same circuit. It does not test the circuit's own faithfulness, completeness or minimality (V1), and nothing on V2, V3, V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that HAP is at least 46% faster than EP with comparable faithfulness. They add that it preserves S-inhibition heads that EAP drops at high sparsity. They say this challenges the view that the speed-faithfulness trade-off is fundamental.
record.recipe_differences: Uses EAP attribution scores to narrow the graph and initialize EP edge pruning, rather than the original study's circuit-discovery and head-level causal tests.
record.method_sensitivity: S-inhibition-head recovery differs between EAP at high sparsity and HAP using a generous attribution threshold followed by EP pruning.

fits_no_version.finding: Faithfulness of the automatically discovered circuits to the full model: logit difference 3.13 for EAP, 3.48 for EP and 3.42 for HAP; KL 0.190 for EP and 0.188 for HAP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Faithfulness of automatically discovered IOI circuits (not the manual circuit) to GPT-2 small, by discovery method.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The experiments cover only GPT-2 Small and IOI. The authors note that generated training-data variation may cause minor differences across runs. The S-inhibition result is qualitative, with no direct head-specific causal patching reported. The supplied flattened Table 1 makes some metric-value assignments unclear.
record.rows_left_out: Runtime values were not recorded as rows because they do not measure the claimed IOI behavior or circuit components. Table 1 metric assignments are recorded only where the flattened text supports preserving the reported values without guessing their column mapping.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not tested. The manual circuit is used only as a reference.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no test for backup heads.
Only GPT-2 small; no other models, sizes, checkpoints or tasks.
Recovery of head classes other than S-inhibition is not reported in text. Ablation types and metrics are not varied. ACDC and other methods are not run.
Ablation, metric and prompt distribution are not varied.
No results split by name order (BABA/ABBA), template or number of names.

missing.what: The exact definition of 'accuracy' against the manual circuit (edge overlap? head overlap?). Recovery or non-recovery of the other head classes (name movers, duplicate-token, induction etc.) shown in Figure 1 but not described in the text.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 was misaligned in the record. The correct mapping is: 94±0.5% = sparsity for all methods; Accuracy 0.698/0.772/0.759; Logit Diff 3.13/3.48/3.42; KL –/0.190/0.188; Runtime 4/2921/1579 s. This mapping is confirmed by the prose ordering and by the 46% speedup (1579 vs 2921). The S-inhibition evidence is qualitative, from figures. This is primarily a methods paper on one model and one task.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit, all stated head roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria head by head; no causal patching of individual heads is reported.
No ablation of main name-mover heads to test backup-head takeover.
Only GPT-2 Small is studied; no other models, sizes, checkpoints, or task reuse are tested.

Compares EAP, EP, and HAP only, and reports a qualitative difference for S-inhibition-head recovery; does not establish equivalence or difference across other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics.
Reports faithfulness metrics but does not vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution to test sensitivity or the claim that the circuit explains only part of the behavior.
Uses IOI templates and mentions BABA and ABBA patterns, but does not report component-level results separately by name order, template, or number of names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Reported circuit-quality values for EAP; supplied table alignment does not securely identify each value's metric.
rows.note: The supplied flattened table does not unambiguously align these values with the Logit Diff and KL columns.
rows.check: The values can be assigned: Accuracy 0.698 and Logit Diff 3.13 (KL '–', runtime 4 s). The prose confirms the ordering: HAP beats EAP and is slightly below EP. Accuracy is computed against the Wang et al. manual circuit as reference, so about 70% agreement at 94% sparsity is partial recovery. The logit difference measures faithfulness of the EAP circuit itself and does not bear on V4.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Table 1 reports lower KL for HAP (0.188) than EP (0.190), contradicting the prose's claim that HAP is slightly worse on both faithfulness metrics; reference accuracy has no explicit formula or denominator.

statements.correction: GPT-2 Small, 117M; HAP preserves heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10 after low-threshold EAP followed by EP; Table 1 sparsity 94±0.5%; GPU and target sparsity controlled; no recovery or performance error bars reported.
statements.problem: Head identities and recovery are correct. Reported uncertainty is only a sparsity range, not uncertainty on recovery or performance. The blanket assertion that controls are absent overlooks the controlled GPU and target sparsity comparison.
